read_first: This is SpicyStock's daily brief: one evening publication's model output, derived from that publication's record and its pick ledger, with the model-record block the same evening run computed from its own bars carried in (section 10), and from nothing else, for an outside analyst to read in place of the full record.
Check that it is current before using it: `status` must be `derived`, and the freshness rule in section 2 (`service.freshness_rule`) is applied with your own clock.
Only the rows in section 5 (`tickets`) are published model tickets. Every other row is research only: its levels are reference arithmetic and SpicyStock offers no order for it.
SpicyStock places, cancels and observes no order and reads no brokerage account. The owner decides and places every order.

delivery.sentence: Published 1:58 AM ET on Tue 24 Nov, 583.4 minutes after the measured session's completion (4:15 PM ET); after both scheduled slots (6:16 PM and 8:16 PM ET); before the next session's open (Tue 24 Nov, 9:30 AM ET).

freshness_rule: Freshness is the reader's own computation: this file carries no clock. Compare your own clock, as an instant with its UTC offset, with the instants in `service.expected`, in this order, and stop at the first that holds.

1. Before `completion_at`: `newest`. The next session has not completed, so no record of a later session can exist yet. The same session can still be published again, and a later run can withdraw a ticket: before acting on a ticket, fetch the file again and compare `identity.canonical.sha256` with the copy the plan was built on.
2. Before `primary_slot_at`: `not_due`. The next session has completed and its evening run is not yet due.
3. Before `retry_slot_at`: `pending`. The first scheduled slot has passed and the retry slot has not.
4. Before `recovery_until`: `late`. Both scheduled slots have passed; a delayed run can still publish the next session until that instant.

5. Otherwise: `missing`. The service does not publish a session after the session that follows it has opened. If this is still the newest file the site serves, the next session was not published and every ticket in this file is expired.

From step 2 on, fetch the file again before relying on it: a newer one may exist. A field that is null has its reason in `service.expected.unknown`; without the instant a step needs, freshness is unknown and the file is research only.
Freshness is not permission. A ticket applies only from `identity.entry_window.opens_at` to its `cutoff_at`; after the cutoff it is over, whatever state this rule gives.

receipt.rule: A morning receipt belongs to this publication only when its `publication.data_sha256` equals `identity.canonical.sha256`. One generated before `window_opens_at` carries no quote from inside the entry window. The receipt is not part of this file: it lands the next morning, if a morning check runs.

near_line.note: the band is this project's own label bound, the largest later re-reading of a published ratio seen through 17 November 2026; it is not a rule and gates nothing

scaling.note: Count thresholds are the reference count times the stocks measured over the reference universe; that scaling is this project's own. Ratio thresholds are not scaled.

market.history_rule: the newest 10 sessions of the record's own breadth history, each read again tonight over tonight's stocks: an earlier session's counts can differ from what its own night published

Risk per trade: $150.00 (0.5% of $30,000.00; his band is 0.25-1%).
Position cap: $7,500.00 (25% of equity) in any one name.
Max 4 open positions (100% of equity if all are at the cap).
Cash reuse: US stock trades generally settle T+1; a sale does not establish immediately spendable cash. Check availability and any cash-account restrictions with your broker.
Cash-account planning reference: no leverage is assumed. The site does not read your broker's settled cash or buying power; confirm available settled cash before each buy.
Plan a protective stop-market order as soon as the buy fills; verify your broker supports the intended entry and linked stop orders. Gaps and slippage can make the loss exceed planned risk.
account.meaning: the model's configured sizing assumptions; not a brokerage balance

candidates.definition: reaction candidates whose mechanical grade is in the trade band (A+, A), with no quality veto, that the discovery admission admits; plus any other name with a published ticket or a selected chart review
candidates.order: published tickets, then names selected for a chart review, then the rest; each in the record's rank order (grade, score descending, ticker)
candidates.model_status: a row is `TICKET` only when the record published a model ticket for it (its order is in `tickets`); every other row is `RESEARCH ONLY: no SpicyStock ticket`
candidates.would_pass_note: the gates after the market gate, re-derived from the row's recorded fields so a RED night does not hide them; passing them is not a ticket: the stop rule, the event registry, sizing and the slot allocation follow, and the market gate stands
candidates.compact_note: every compact row is RESEARCH ONLY: its mechanical grade is in the trade band, it has no veto, the admission admits it and the chart reader did not read it; under YELLOW the band is A+ only

near_volume_boundary.meaning: the burst's volume is within this fraction of the previous session's, so its higher-volume check can flip on the provider's later corrections; the bound is this project's own label, not a rule

checklist.label: not up two days in a row
checklist.threshold: up_run <= 1, counting days above +1.0%; veto at 3+ up closes of any size

checklist.label: linearity of the prior leg
checklist.threshold: ER >= 0.4 or R2 >= 0.55 (both for A+); failing is a veto

checklist.label: young trend: first or second breakout
checklist.threshold: prior breakouts since the move started <= 1 (0 for A+)

checklist.label: narrow or negative day before
checklist.threshold: prior day negative or range < 2.0% (A+: negative and under its 20-session median range)

checklist.label: consolidation quality
checklist.threshold: base 3-20 sessions, breakdowns <= 1, giveback <= 0.34, tightness <= 1.0 (A+: 0 breakdowns, 0 bursts inside, giveback <= 0.25, tightness <= 0.7, base volume under the leg's and the 50-session average)

checklist.label: close near the high
checklist.threshold: close_pos >= 0.8 and close > open (A+ >= 0.9; partial from 0.7)

checklist.label: range expansion
checklist.threshold: today's range over the largest of the prior 5 >= 1.0 (A+: also over the prior 10)

checklist.label: higher volume
checklist.threshold: volume > prior session (A+: rank <= 3 of the last 60); a base over 21 sessions also needs >= 1.5x the 50-session average

candidates.check_marks: letter then + (pass at the A+ level), nothing (pass), ~ (partial), x (fail), ? (not measured)

exit_rules.when: same or next day, the price reaches the sell-half level (+8% from the planned entry)
exit_rules.rule: sell half and move the stop to 25-50 cents under that day's high

exit_rules.when: any single day closes at or above the abnormal-close level (+10%)
exit_rules.rule: take at least partial profit and move the stop up to protect the rest

exit_rules.when: it opens at or above the gap-exit level (+20%) after entry

exit_rules.rule: the stop rises to the entry day's low if that is above the stop
sell at least half at the close

exit_rules.when: day 3 closes at or below the planned entry

exit_rules.rule: raise the stop to each day's low (it never moves down)

exit_rules.when: the protective stop at the stop is a stop-market order, live intraday from the moment the buy fills
exit_rules.rule: if it is somehow not filled, exit on any close below it

do not move the stop to break-even before day 5 just because it is green (theStrat Lab EP9M backtest: the win rate collapses from 29.8% to 7.25%; delaying to day 5 restores it); the +8% raise above is a different rule

labels.booked: what the model books: a stop first reached inside a session at exactly the stop price, and a session that opens at or under the stop at its open
labels.at_close: the same exit at that session's close: what holding to the close would have been, and not a fill estimate
labels.at_low: the same exit at that session's low: a worst-case bound for a stop order filled that day
labels.minute: where that session's minute bars are retained, the first minute at or under the stop: a stop order filled inside that minute would be between its low and the stop

definitions: A ticket is one night's order for one stock. The scorecard counts every retained ticket once.

A setup is a chain of tickets of one ticker and kind: a ticket continues the chain when it was issued within 5 sessions after the ticket before it and that one has no fill known (not filled, awaiting its first session, or without bars). A setup's bucket is its last ticket's.
An era is the tickets sized against one model account (equity and risk percent).

R is a settled ticket's model result over its risk at the model entry (the entry less the published stop, on the whole position), every sale weighted by the whole shares it sold. It counts each ticket as one unit whatever its size.
Model dollars are a settled ticket's sale prices less its model entry, times the shares sold.
sentences: The model record counts 22 tickets issued from 2026-10-08 through 2026-11-13: 17 distinct setups, and 5 tickets that issued a setup again on a later night.
By ticket: 5 settled, 1 uncertain, 14 not filled, 2 missing or stale bars. By setup: 5 settled, 1 uncertain, 10 not filled, 1 missing or stale bars.

Issued more than once: OGN anticipation 2 times (2026-10-27 to 2026-10-28); MFIC anticipation 4 times (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13); UTZ anticipation 2 times (2026-11-10 to 2026-11-11). No ticket that was later issued again has a fill known, so re-issues raise the ticket counts and add nothing to the sum of R.
The 5 settled tickets sum to +0.43R (2 wins, 3 losses, 0 breakeven). Below 20 settled tickets the record prints no rate.

The tickets were sized against 3 model accounts: $10,000 at 0.5% risk (2 tickets, 1 settled, +0.41R, +$2.24 in model dollars); $2,000 at 0.5% risk (8 tickets, 1 settled, +3.02R, +$5.25 in model dollars); $30,000 at 0.5% risk (12 tickets, 3 settled, -3.00R, -$90.63 in model dollars).
A sum of R is not a sum of dollars: R counts each ticket as one unit whatever its size. The settled tickets sum to +0.43R and to -$83.14 in model dollars.

3 settled tickets ended on a stop. As the model books them, a stop first reached inside a session at exactly the stop price, the sum is -3.00R (-$90.63). With the same exits at the stop day's close it is -4.66R (-$140.78): what holding to the close would have been, not a fill estimate. At the stop day's low, a worst-case bound, it is -5.78R (-$174.64).
Under those readings the settled sum is +0.43R as booked, -1.23R at the closes and -2.35R at the lows.
VIK 2026-11-04: the retained minute bars first reach the stop at 09:58 ET, in a minute that opened at $88.26 with a low of $88.09; at that low the ticket reads -1.03R.

2 settled tickets held 1 share and sold it whole at the half-sale step, because 1 share cannot be halved: SN +0.41R, EXEL +3.02R. Walked over the same bars at 2 shares: SN +0.22R, EXEL +2.62R. With those readings the settled sum is -0.16R.

1 ticket is uncertain: the bars cannot say whether it filled, and it is in no sum. MCS 2026-10-28 reads -0.91R if filled at its $28.75 limit and -0.88R if filled at its $28.47 trigger. These are bounds, not results.
3 counted tickets were withdrawn by a later run of their own session and stay in the record and in these counts: MG 2026-10-08, SN 2026-10-08 (settled, +0.41R), ZIM 2026-10-09.
limits: A model from bars alone, not a brokerage record: no fees, spread, slippage, tax or real execution is measured, and nothing here knows what anyone holds.
Minute bars are retained only for a first day the daily bar could not place, so a stop day usually has its daily bar alone and its range stays between that day's low and the stop.
A ticket's account is the publishing record's own, the previous brief's for the same evidence id, or the seed read off the publications in git; an account none of them gives is not guessed.

rules.digest_note: the record's digest nests the universe membership identity, so it moves on any night the selection's membership moves; `digest_without_membership` is the same digest with that identity removed, and moves only when an archived rule changes

limits: This is a model's output from one provider's daily bars. This brief places and observes no order, and SpicyStock reads no brokerage account, balance, position or fill.

No price here is a live quote. A candidate's prices are the measured session's bar as published; an open plan's, the pick ledger's and the model record's are the earlier sessions' the rows name. Check the current price, spread and halt state before acting.
A grade is a checklist score over daily bars and, where a review is recorded, one chart reader's judgement. It is not a forecast.
The model record establishes no edge. Its counts are model plans walked on bars, not trades; read `scorecard.readable` and its counts before any rate, and a sum of R is not a sum of dollars.

A model fill at the open assumes a buy stop-limit order already resting at the broker before the open. Whether the broker accepts that order for a burst ticket, whose buy stop is the last close, is unconfirmed.
A stop reached inside a session is booked at exactly the stop price. A real stop order fills at the next available price, which can be worse, and a gap through the stop loses more.

Research levels are never tickets. For a burst they are what the record's own plan rule gives for the recorded bar at the archived model account; for a setting-up row they are the record's own plan, which the plan rule may have refused (`plan_rule_eligible` false) or left without shares. No chart review accepted them unless the row's reader state says so.
A model ticket is sized for the archived model account (`account`), not for the reader's account. Shares, cost and risk are planned price-to-stop arithmetic at the limit, not a maximum loss.

The market regime is SpicyStock's gate for its own model tickets: an input to weigh, not an instruction. The scaling of its count thresholds, the admission rule, the checklist weights and the chart reader are this project's own rules (knowledge/method.md says whose number each is), and the record does not establish that the gate improves outcomes.

SpicyStock reads no company news. Earnings and SEC 8-K items are read for published tickets only, from SEC filings: a projected date is an estimate, never an announced date, unknown is never clear, and filings are not news coverage.
The event registry is a hand-kept list of known cash acquisitions. A stock that is not in it has not been cleared: issuer news, offerings, guidance and other corporate events are not checked.

One provider's bars as of the run's fetch; a session's volume can be revised afterwards. The universe is the selection named in `service.universe`, not point-in-time membership, and a stock named stale had no bar for the session: its inputs are unknown, not a measured non-match.
Whether the broker accepts the printed order form (a day buy stop-limit with a one-triggers-the-other sell stop) is unconfirmed; see knowledge/broker-fidelity.md.
Rows are bounded. `bounds` states every list that was cut, how many rows were left out and the rule that chose the kept ones; the canonical record carries every row.

This brief is bound to one publication by the SHA-256 and byte length in `identity.canonical`. Whether a newer publication exists is not in this file: apply `service.freshness_rule` with your own clock.

research_tail.meaning: Every other reaction candidate: RESEARCH ONLY, no SpicyStock ticket and no levels. Tickers in the record's rank order, grouped by the one reason; a ticker whose final grade differs from its mechanical grade shows both

groups.reason: mechanical grade B, below the trade band
mechanical grade C, below the trade band
mechanical grade skip, below the trade band

bounds.candidates_rule: Tickets and reviewed names are always detailed; of the rest, in the stated order, the largest multiple of 4 (or all) is detailed that keeps brief.json within 250000 bytes, and the others are compact rows; only if none can be detailed are compact rows cut, to the largest multiple of 10 that fits, the rest moving to the research tail
bounds.research_tail_rule: the first 4000: the admitted trade-band names moved out for size, then the rest by the record's rank order
bounds.open_plans_rule: the first 24 in the record's own order
bounds.stale_names_rule: the first 25 in the record's own order
bounds.also_quiet_rule: the first 10 in the record's own order
bounds.breadth_history_rule: the newest 10 sessions of the record's own breadth history
bounds.model_record_rule: The evening run's model-record block is carried whole when its canonical encoding is within 60000 bytes and the brief still fits with it; past that bound it is carried reduced (each plan row keeps its identity, result and account; the setups table is left out), and not at all if that does not fit either; brief.md prints its sentences and, while they fit, the first 30 rows and 12 columns of each of its tables
bounds.text_rule: A copied sentence over 900 characters is cut and ends with an ellipsis
